- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots in the next few days; apply a mild downward correction (e.g., -0.5 to -1.5%).
- If sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.3), model underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent highs; apply a lagged smoothing rule: if last 3–5 days are rising, cap forecast growth to avoid overextension.
- In periods of high sentiment volatility, model tends to misalign with true mean; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 7–10 days as anchor.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage mean reversion; adjust final 5–7 days downward if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
